shapes.name: RegexRuleCondition
shapes.doc: Deterministic rule chaining (vaud-engine-only, R2X): run the carrying rule only when the rule named by `ruleId` DID (`matched: true`) or DID NOT (`matched: false`) apply earlier in the same pass. One pass, sortOrder order: a condition naming a rule that has not run yet (or does not exist) skips the carrying rule with an honest trace reason - never forward-resolves.

shapes.name: RegexRule
shapes.doc: One find/replace rule. `find`/`flags` are stored SEPARATELY (the Risu/RC/Lumi encoding); the SillyTavern codec folds/unfolds its single `/pattern/flags` wire string on import/export (the lorebook `keywordToTrigger` precedent). `flags` is stored VERBATIM, including Risu extension tokens observed live (e.g. "gu<cbs>") - never stripped except at compile time inside the engine (core/regex/apply.ts), never here.

fields.name: id
fields.meaning: stable rule id, preserved across round-trips

fields.name: note
fields.meaning: internal creator note; distinct from label (Lumiverse `description`)

fields.name: find
fields.meaning: bare pattern, NO delimiters

fields.name: flags
fields.meaning: verbatim flags string; default "g"; may carry non-JS extension tokens

fields.name: useFlags
fields.meaning: Risu `ableFlag`: whether the custom flags string applies

fields.name: replace
fields.meaning: verbatim; may carry $1/{{match}}/CBS/HTML - render only through SealedHtmlPreview

fields.name: trimStrings
fields.meaning: ST/RC/Lumi: fragments stripped from the match before replace

fields.name: targets
fields.meaning: Lumiverse's placement x target matrix; absent = platform default

fields.name: substituteFind
fields.meaning: find-side macro substitution mode; absent = "none"

fields.name: minDepth
fields.meaning: ST/RC/Lumi/Marinara depth window (message depth, 0 = most recent - exact counting per platform is an R1 residual, see REGEX-FORMATS.md)

fields.name: runOnEdit
fields.meaning: ST/RC/Lumi: re-apply this rule when a message is edited

fields.name: characterIds
fields.meaning: Marinara `targetCharacterIds`: limit to specific recipient characters; empty/absent = all

fields.name: firstMatchOnly
fields.meaning: Vaud-engine-only (R2X, no wire home anywhere - travel lint marks these three under every platform lens; export keeps the data canonical-side and emits nothing): replace only the FIRST match even under a global flag.

fields.name: condition
fields.meaning: Vaud-engine-only: run only when another rule in this set did (or did not) apply this pass.

fields.name: overlay
fields.meaning: Vaud-engine-only: display-channel rule that returns match spans + replacement as an OVERLAY instead of mutating text (ST names this "Overlay strategy" and implements it nowhere).

fields.name: extras
fields.meaning: Per-platform leftovers with no first-class home (Lumi telemetry/scope/script_id, ST id/uuid, ...). Sealed, round-trips untouched - the lossless-escrow doctrine.

fields.name: enabled
fields.meaning: Set-level on/off (the Library shelf's enable switch; the lorebook `enabled?` precedent). Absent = on; always read as `enabled !== false`. An off set skips export the way an off lorebook does. Additive and optional so the risu character codec and the in-flight set editor stay compatible.

shapes.name: CharacterRegexScript
shapes.doc: Narrow character-card view of a regex rule: the Risu `customScripts` legacy shape (singular `phase`, no id/enabled/sortOrder - the card wire has none of those). `entities/character/schema.ts` re-exports this as its `RegexScript` so there is one definition, not two independently-maintained shapes (REGEX-JEWEL-PLAN.md R0). It is intentionally NOT `RegexRule` itself: `RegexRule.phases` is an array and requires `id`/`enabled`/`sortOrder`, which would silently change `CharacterBehavior.regexScripts`'s wire contract and break the risu codec's round-trip tests (`src/formats/risu/risu.test.ts`, out of this phase's scope) - reality over a literal full alias. `RegexRule` is what the standalone regex entity (and its editor) uses; this stays the small card-embedded twin until a real migration replaces `customScripts` with regex-entity refs.

fields.name: phase
fields.meaning: pipeline phase, open union: "edittrans" | "editoutput" | "editdisplay" | ...

fields.name: flags
fields.meaning: custom regex flags (Risu `flag`)

fields.name: useFlags
fields.meaning: whether the custom flags apply (Risu `ableFlag`)
